o: each paragraph visibly advances the thesis in a logical sequence
the essay is exactly five paragraphs
the thesis appears in every paragraph
quiz.e: Readers can follow how the claims build toward the conclusion.

quiz.q: 'Concede-then-counter' phrasing looks like:
o: 'While it is true that X, it does not follow that Y'
'X, Y, and Z are all true'
quiz.e: It acknowledges the point, then limits its force.

quiz.q: Ending an argument essay by answering 'so what?' means:
o: explaining why the argument matters beyond the essay
quiz.e: A strong close conveys the stakes and significance.

quiz.q: A nuanced thesis such as 'Curfews reduce some crimes but at a civic cost' is preferable to a flat one because it:
o: reflects the complexity of the issue and is easier to defend well
is safer because it avoids a position
quiz.e: Qualified, specific claims tend to support stronger reasoning.

quiz.q: Two independent clauses joined only by a comma form a:
quiz.e: Fix a comma splice with a period, a semicolon, or a coordinating conjunction.

quiz.q: 'She likes hiking, swimming, and to bike' violates:
quiz.e: The items in a series must match in form: 'hiking, swimming, and biking'.

quiz.q: A colon is correctly used when:
o: the clause before it is complete and it introduces an explanation, list, or appositive
it joins two independent clauses casually
it replaces a comma in a series
quiz.e: 'She had one goal: to finish.' The clause before the colon stands alone.

quiz.q: A semicolon between two independent clauses signals that they are:
quiz.e: 'The evidence was thin; the conclusion was bold.'

quiz.q: On a multiple-choice 'writing' revision question, the best answer is usually the one that is:
quiz.e: AP MC writing items reward economy and precision.

quiz.q: 'In order to reduce costs' can most often be tightened to:
o: 'With the goal that costs are reduced'
quiz.e: 'In order to' is usually padding for 'to'.

quiz.q: On MC reading questions, an answer choice should be:
o: verifiable against the actual text of the passage
the one that matches your opinion
quiz.e: Always confirm the choice with specific wording in the passage.

quiz.q: 'The committee released their report' has an error in:
quiz.e: Collective nouns like 'committee' are usually treated as singular in formal American usage.

quiz.q: A dash is best used to:
o: set off an emphatic interruption or addition
introduce a formal list (a colon does that)
quiz.e: Overusing dashes reduces their emphatic effect.

quiz.q: 'Past history' and 'end result' are examples of:
quiz.e: History is already past; a result is already an end. Cut the redundant word.

quiz.q: Which is the ONLY Hawthorne work on the Unit 1 exam?
quiz.e: The class schedule says "Young Goodman Brown" is the only Hawthorne work on Unit 1; "The Custom House" and The Scarlet Letter belong to the Unit 2 exam.

quiz.q: On the class schedule, what is the date of the Unit 1 exam?
quiz.e: The Unit 1 Exam: Great American Short Stories is scheduled for Tue 10/6.

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT fair game on the Unit 1 exam?
quiz.e: Emerson, Keats and the Irving / Romanticism packet are all fair game. The Scarlet Letter is saved for Unit 2.

quiz.q: Which movement values emotion, imagination, nature and the individual over reason and order?
quiz.e: Romanticism reacted against Enlightenment rationalism and Neoclassical order.

quiz.q: "Rip Van Winkle" was written by:
quiz.e: Irving published it in The Sketch Book (1819-20).

quiz.q: In "Rip Van Winkle", Rip's 20-year sleep spans which historical change?
o: British colonial rule to the new American republic
The Civil War years to the era of Reconstruction and rebuilding
The Puritan era of Salem to the years of the witch trials
The Gilded Age of railroads to the Progressive Era reforms
quiz.e: He falls asleep under King George III and wakes after the American Revolution, when Washington's portrait and the flag have replaced the old symbols.

quiz.q: Irving portrays Dame Van Winkle mainly as:
o: A shrewish, nagging wife who makes Rip's life harder
A loving partner who shares Rip's adventures
A powerful village leader who commands the men of the community
A mysterious spirit of the mountains who guides Rip
quiz.e: Irving's diction (termagant, virago) casts Dame as a scold and invites sympathy for Rip.

quiz.q: Who is the fictional historian said to have left the papers behind "Rip Van Winkle"?
quiz.e: Knickerbocker is the framing historian; Geoffrey Crayon is Irving's pen name for The Sketch Book.

quiz.q: Irving uses Rip's long sleep mainly to:
o: Comment on how the nation and its politics have changed
Prove that the Dutch settlers of the valley could be trusted with property
Warn readers about the dangers of mountain travel
Mock the customs of the Hudson Valley's oldest families
quiz.e: The time jump lets Irving show Revolution-era change through Rip's confusion, aiming his purpose at the new nation and its identity.

quiz.q: Which appeal does Irving trigger by showing Rip as put-upon and good-natured?
quiz.e: The sympathetic portrait draws emotion (pathos) from readers.

quiz.q: "The Eve of St. Agnes" was written by:
quiz.e: Keats wrote it in 1819; it was published in 1820.

quiz.q: How many stanzas does "The Eve of St. Agnes" have?
quiz.e: The class schedule assigns stanzas 1-42.

quiz.q: A Spenserian stanza has how many lines and which rhyme scheme?
o: Fourteen lines, ABAB CDCD EFEF GG
quiz.e: Keats uses the nine-line Spenserian stanza.

quiz.q: According to the St. Agnes legend, what might a young woman see if she follows the rituals on St. Agnes' Eve?
o: Her future husband in a dream
quiz.e: The legend promises a dream vision of a future husband.

quiz.q: Who sneaks into Madeline's chamber in Keats's poem?
quiz.e: Porphyro, from a hostile family, hides in her room with Angela's help.

quiz.q: Who is the old woman who helps Porphyro?
quiz.e: Angela is the old nurse who lets Porphyro in.

quiz.q: Which device does Keats rely on to make the poem feel rich and sensuous?
quiz.e: The feast, colors and warm/cold contrasts are built from imagery.

quiz.q: Who wrote "The Fall of the House of Usher"?
quiz.e: Poe published it in 1839.

quiz.q: How does the narrator first feel about the House of Usher?
o: A sense of insufferable gloom and dread
Delighted by its beauty and its old grounds
Indifferent to the house after his long trip
Curious about its history and its old family
quiz.e: The opening imagery (dull, dark, soundless day; eye-like windows) creates gloom.

quiz.q: Which words/devices in the opening scene create the gloom of the house?
o: Imagery and diction such as “dull, dark, soundless” and “vacant eye-like windows”
Rapid dialogue and sharp humor between two old friends meeting again
A list of dates and precise measurements of the whole estate and grounds
Exaggerated comparisons that turn the crumbling setting into a joke for readers
quiz.e: Poe's word choice builds a gloomy mood, and the eye-like windows personify the house.

quiz.q: Which is an example of personification in "The Fall of the House of Usher"?
quiz.e: Giving the house eyes personifies an inanimate object.

quiz.q: What is Madeline to Roderick?
quiz.e: Madeline is Roderick's twin sister, who is wasting away.

quiz.q: What is "The Haunted Palace" in relation to the story?
o: A poem within the story that mirrors Roderick's mind and the house's fall
A real palace that the narrator visits before reaching the House of Usher
A poem Madeline wrote to be read at her own funeral by the family
A book of ghost stories that Roderick keeps in the family library
quiz.e: It tells how a fair palace of Thought is overrun by evil, echoing the Usher tragedy.

quiz.q: What is the "Mad Trist" in the story?
o: A romance read aloud whose noises seem to echo real sounds in the house
A song Roderick sings to soothe himself as the storm rises at midnight
A legal document that leaves the house and its estate to the narrator
A journal in which Madeline records the progress of her illness
quiz.e: The narrator reads the tale of Ethelred; the sounds in it match events in the house, foreshadowing Madeline's return.

quiz.q: How does the story end for the House of Usher?
o: The house splits apart and sinks into the tarn
The narrator inherits the house and moves in
Roderick recovers and restores the family name
Madeline leaves the house for a new life in Europe
quiz.e: The fissure widens and the house collapses into the tarn.

quiz.q: Which genre best describes "The Fall of the House of Usher"?
quiz.e: Gloomy setting, decay, madness and death mark it as Gothic.

quiz.q: Who wrote "Baker's Bluejay Yarn"?
quiz.e: Twain wrote it in 1880 in A Tramp Abroad.

quiz.q: What is a yarn?
o: A long tale of adventure or incredible happenings, often exaggerated
A brief moral story that ends with a proverb about honest work
A serious eyewitness report of a historical event by a soldier
A comic poem written in rhymed couplets for a popular audience
quiz.e: The class schedule defines yarn as a tale of adventure or incredible happenings.

quiz.q: The bluejays in Baker's story talk and act like people. That is:
quiz.e: Animate beings (animals) with human traits is anthropomorphism.

quiz.q: Which is the best definition of personification?
o: Giving animals or other living creatures human characteristics
Comparing two unlike things using the words like or as
Repeating a beginning sound in words close together
quiz.e: Personification applies to nonliving things; anthropomorphism to living beings.

quiz.q: What does juxtaposition mean?
o: Putting two things side by side for effect
Repeating a key word again and again for emphasis
Using exaggeration to make a humorous point
Naming a historical event to connect a story to it
quiz.e: Contrasting elements next to each other highlight their differences.

quiz.q: Who is telling the tale of the bluejay and the knothole?
o: Jim Baker, in his own voice, inside Twain's frame
Twain, speaking as an omniscient narrator without a frame
The first bluejay, describing his own mistake later
An unnamed miner who overheard the jays
quiz.e: Baker's dialect-rich voice tells the yarn, indirectly characterizing him.

quiz.q: How does Twain indirectly characterize Jim Baker?
o: Through his folksy speech, sincere claims and exaggerated stories
Through a direct statement by the narrator that he is a dishonest man
Through the opinions of the other miners in the region who know him
Through a description of his clothes and his cabin's furniture
quiz.e: Indirect characterization comes from what a character says and does.

quiz.q: What might the jay's effort to fill the hole in the roof represent, according to the class question?
o: A metaphor for foolish or futile human effort
A symbol of the miners' long and hopeless search for buried gold
A warning about the danger of leaving empty houses in the mountains
An allegory of the terrible costs of the Civil War for ordinary people
quiz.e: The class schedule asks to what extent it relays a metaphor for human existence.

quiz.q: Which years does the class schedule ask you to research for context to "Baker's Bluejay Yarn"?
quiz.e: Twain lived 1835-1910 and the story appeared in 1880, so students researched 1835-1880.

quiz.q: "Young Goodman Brown" is set in:
o: The Catskill Mountains of New York
Victorian London during the industrial age
quiz.e: Brown lives in Salem Village and journeys into the forest.

quiz.q: In "Young Goodman Brown", who or what is Faith?
o: Brown's wife and a symbol of his religious faith
Brown's sister, who follows him into the forest
The name of the meeting-house where he prays
The traveler's nickname for the forest path
quiz.e: The name works as an allegory, and Faith's pink ribbons appear in the woods.

quiz.q: The traveler's staff that resembles a black serpent is an allusion to:
quiz.e: The serpent staff alludes to the serpent in Eden and marks the traveler as the devil.

quiz.q: Why does Hawthorne include so many Biblical allusions?
o: To deepen the moral and spiritual stakes for readers who recognize the source
To prove that the events of the story took place in Biblical times
To make the traveler seem like a real historical figure from Salem
To show that Brown has memorized the whole Bible and can quote it
quiz.e: An allusion is a passing reference that depends on the reader's knowledge.

quiz.q: What effect does the story's ending have on Brown?
o: He becomes stern, sad and distrustful for the rest of his life
He grows more devout and becomes a respected deacon of the church
He forgives his neighbors and finds a lasting peace with Faith
He leaves Salem to start a new life elsewhere
quiz.e: Brown returns from the forest unable to trust anyone.

quiz.q: What is the central ambiguity in "Young Goodman Brown"?
o: Whether the forest events were a dream or real
Whether Faith remained loyal to Brown all night
Whether the traveler was truly Brown's grandfather
Whether Salem was safe for travelers after dark
quiz.e: Hawthorne leaves it open.

quiz.q: Which is Hawthorne's attitude toward Puritans in this story?
o: Critical of their hypocrisy and rigid gloom
Admiring of their piety and strict discipline
Neutral, like a historian recording facts
Playful, treating their beliefs as a comic subject
quiz.e: The story exposes hypocrisy in the community's most respected figures.

quiz.q: Which sequence of authors matches the order Rip, Usher, Baker, Goodman Brown?
quiz.e: Rip Van Winkle: Irving; Usher: Poe; Baker's Bluejay Yarn: Twain; Young Goodman Brown: Hawthorne.

quiz.q: In the Emerson excerpt, the materialist mainly starts from
o: The external world and respect for society and social institutions
The mind's own consciousness and its inner intuition about reality
Religious visions that override the ordinary evidence of experience
The idea that nature, literature and history are only dreams
quiz.e: The excerpt says the materialist "takes his departure from the external world" and respects society, government, luxury and every mass; the idealist starts from consciousness.

quiz.q: Emerson is best known as a leader of:
quiz.e: Emerson led American Transcendentalism.

quiz.q: Who popularized the term "American Dream" in The Epic of America (1931)?
quiz.e: Adams defined it as a dream of a better, richer, fuller life for everyone with opportunity by ability.

quiz.q: Which is the best pivotal question?
o: To what extent does Irving's language suggest he favors one sex over another?
What is the name of the dog that follows Rip up into the mountains?
In what year did Washington Irving first write “Rip Van Winkle” in England?
How many years does Rip sleep in the Kaatskill Mountains before waking?
quiz.e: Pivotal questions are open-ended and text-based, not hunt-and-fetch.

quiz.q: What should you do with a multi-part question, according to the class directions?
o: Answer in one cohesive response with evidence for each part
Answer each part separately in short bullet lists, with no linking
Answer only the first part in detail and skim the remaining parts
Give all the evidence once at the end, without any transitions
quiz.e: The class schedule tells you to answer multi-part questions cohesively with evidence for every subquestion.

quiz.q: The class schedule defines an allusion as:
o: A brief, indirect reference to a person, place, thing or idea of historical, cultural, literary or political significance
A long, direct retelling of an earlier story inside a new story, with full quotations from the older source and an explanation of it
A word whose sound imitates the noise it names, like “buzz” or “crash”, used to give a poem a vivid sound for readers
A comparison between two unlike things that uses the words “like” or “as” to show how they are similar in one way
quiz.e: It relies on the reader's prior knowledge.

quiz.q: Class question: How does Washington Irving use characterization to develop a central idea in “Rip Van Winkle”? Which response is best?
o: By pairing a beloved, easygoing Rip with a scolding Dame, Irving builds sympathy for freedom from duty and comments on a changing society
By describing Rip as a brave, patriotic soldier whose courage wins the Revolution for the colonies and earns him honor
By making Dame Van Winkle the hero and Rip the villain in order to teach a lesson about hard work and duty
By giving the reader almost no description of Rip so that the setting alone can carry the theme of the story
quiz.e: Irving's diction ("termagant", "virago") and Rip's warm reception by children and dogs shape reader sympathy and connect to the story's comment on change.

quiz.q: Class question: For what reasons does Hawthorne use allusion in “Young Goodman Brown”? Which response is best?
o: Biblical references such as the serpent-like staff give the forest journey the weight of temptation and sin for readers who recognize them
Biblical references prove the story is a true historical record of a real night that happened in Salem village long ago
Biblical references are used to entertain readers with a series of comic puns about the Puritans and their ministers
Biblical references replace the need for setting, since readers already know what the woods and the road look like
quiz.e: An allusion is an indirect reference that relies on the reader's knowledge; Hawthorne's Biblical allusions frame Brown's fall.

quiz.q: Class question: In what ways is Poe's use of other works (“The Haunted Palace”, Ethelred's story) significant in “The Fall of the House of Usher”? Which response is best?
o: The poem and the romance mirror and foreshadow Roderick's collapse and the house's fall, and they blur story and reality
The poem and the romance show that Poe was unable to invent an original plot and had to borrow from other writers to fill his story
The poem and the romance explain the full history of the Usher family tree and how the mansion came to be inherited
The poem and the romance prove that the narrator is a professional poet and translator who chose these texts to show his taste
quiz.e: The palace of Thought overrun by evil parallels Roderick, and the noises in the romance echo events in the house.

quiz.q: Class question: What is Twain's intent in telling “Baker's Bluejay Yarn”? Which response is best?
o: To use a comic tall tale about human-like jays to laugh at human foolishness, pride and the way a crowd piles on opinions
To teach readers scientific facts about how bluejays communicate, gather and behave in the wild, using an entertaining example
To argue that the miners of the West are more intelligent and honest than the birds and beasts around them
To describe the events of the Civil War from the lighthearted point of view of a talkative animal narrator
quiz.e: Anthropomorphism, hyperbole and Baker's earnest voice turn a silly story into a mirror of human behavior.

quiz.q: Class question: What is the take-away or thesis Hawthorne intends in “Young Goodman Brown”? Which response is best?
o: Suspicion and the discovery of hypocrisy can destroy faith and a person's ability to trust, whether or not the evil was real
Nature is full of hidden dangers, so travelers should never leave the safety of the village after sunset for any reason
Puritan leaders were models of honesty and courage who deserve the loyalty and trust of every villager in town
Newly married men should always stay at home with their wives on important nights, since a single absence can ruin a marriage
quiz.e: Brown's dying hour is gloom because doubt poisons his relationships, and the story's ambiguity emphasizes that.

quiz.q: Class question: In what ways does the Emerson excerpt reflect themes from the Great American Short Stories unit? Which response is best?
o: The idealist trusts individual consciousness over society, as Brown and Rip do in different ways, and Romantic writers prize the individual mind
The excerpt argues that social class is the only reality, which matches the main idea of every story we read in the unit
The excerpt agrees with the Puritans that the individual has little value apart from the church community and its authority
The excerpt has no connection to the unit at all, because it is a piece of philosophy and not a work of literature
quiz.e: The idealist begins from consciousness and reckons the world an appearance, echoing the Romantic focus on the individual and inner life.

quiz.q: Class question: How did Irving's own life influence his writing? Which response is best supported by the handout?
o: Trips up the Hudson through the Catskills and time in Tarrytown supplied settings, Dutch customs and ghost stories he later used
He spent his whole life in Manhattan and wrote only about the city streets and the merchant families that he knew there
He wrote from his own experience as a soldier at Bunker Hill during the Revolution and drew every plot from that
He avoided real places in his fiction and invented every setting from imagination alone, drawing nothing from his travels
quiz.e: The handout says the Kaatskill Mountains had "the most witching effect on my boyish imagination" and that Tarrytown introduced him to Sleepy Hollow's ghost stories.

quiz.q: Class question: Deconstruct Adams' definition. What does his diction "better and richer and fuller for everyone" suggest?
o: That the dream is about a fuller life and equal opportunity, not only about wealth
That the dream is solely about earning as much money as possible during one's lifetime
That only Europeans and their descendants can achieve the dream in America
That the dream requires a person to be born into a high social position with money
quiz.e: Adams says it is "not a dream of motor cars and high wages merely" but a social order allowing each person to reach their fullest stature.

quiz.q: Which device is present in: “Like pious incense from a censer old” (Keats)?
quiz.e: "Like" makes an explicit comparison between the Beadsman's frosted breath and incense.

quiz.q: Which device is present in: “A sharp tongue is the only edged tool that grows keener with constant use” (Irving, about Dame Van Winkle)?
quiz.e: The tongue is compared directly, without like or as, to a cutting tool.

quiz.q: Which device is present in: “sweating like an ice-pitcher” (the jay in Baker's yarn)?
quiz.e: The comparison uses "like". The jay also displays human behavior (anthropomorphism).

quiz.q: Which device is present in: “There must have been five thousand of them” (the jays gather at the hole)?
o: Irony of appearance and reality only
quiz.e: An exaggeration for humorous effect fits the tall-tale tone.

quiz.q: Which device is present in: “Through which came flowing, flowing, flowing, / And sparkling evermore” (“The Haunted Palace”)?
o: Repetition that creates rhythm and a sense of endless motion
Litotes, an understatement created by negating the opposite of what is meant
Asyndeton, in which conjunctions are left out of a list of related items
Dialect spelling that shows how the different speakers of the poem talk
quiz.e: Repeating "flowing" three times creates sound and rhythm and emphasizes the constant stream of echoes.

quiz.q: Which device is present in: “round and round she goes” repeated throughout Rubin's “The Widow's Walk”?
quiz.e: A refrain is a line repeated for effect, here evoking the widow's endless pacing.

quiz.q: Which device(s) are present in: “a staff, which bore the likeness of a great black snake, so curiously wrought that it might almost be seen to twist and wriggle itself like a living serpent”?
o: Simile and a Biblical allusion (the serpent)
Hyperbole and dialect, showing an exaggerated claim in a regional voice
Onomatopoeia and irony, imitating sounds while saying the opposite of the truth
Apostrophe and epistrophe, addressing an absent person and repeating an ending
quiz.e: "like a living serpent" is a simile and the snake alludes to the serpent in the Genesis story of temptation.

quiz.q: Which device is present in: “the vacant eye-like windows” (Poe)?
o: Anthropomorphism of an animal and hyperbole
quiz.e: The house is given eyes, which is personification, and the words create a strong visual image.

quiz.q: Which device is present in the name Faith for Brown's wife, who leaves him at the door and appears again at the end?
quiz.e: Faith stands both for a person and for his religious faith.

quiz.q: Which device is present in: “The red coat was changed for one of blue and buff, and underneath was painted GENERAL WASHINGTON” (paraphrase of the inn sign in Rip)?
o: Symbolism of the change from British to American rule
Onomatopoeia that imitates the sounds of a tavern
A pun on the words “red” and “blue”
Epistrophe, repeating the last words of successive clauses
quiz.e: The sign's change of uniform and name symbolizes the shift from monarchy to republic that Rip slept through.

quiz.q: In “Rip Van Winkle”, the word “termagant” (describing Dame Van Winkle) most closely means
o: A kind and patient neighbor who helps others in need
A fearful, shy person who avoids other people
A traveling merchant who sells goods door to door
quiz.e: Termagant is used with virago for Dame's scolding temper.

quiz.q: “Virago” most closely means
o: A cheerful storyteller at the inn
A young soldier in the militia
A skilled cook in a Dutch kitchen
quiz.e: Irving pairs it with termagant to characterize Dame.

quiz.q: Rip's “insuperable aversion to all kinds of profitable labor”: “insuperable aversion” most nearly means
o: A slight and passing preference against a task
A temporary illness that prevents work
A legal duty to serve a neighbor
quiz.e: Insuperable means unable to be overcome; aversion is strong dislike.

quiz.q: “Obsequious” most closely means
o: Fawning and overly eager to please
Loud, violent and quick to argue
Sleepy, slow and slow to act
Suspicious, secretive and slow to trust
quiz.e: Irving uses obsequious for someone excessively eager to please.

quiz.q: “Alacrity” most closely means
quiz.e: Alacrity is eager promptness.

quiz.q: “Akimbo” describes arms that are
o: Bent with hands on hips and elbows out
Crossed tightly over the chest in a firm stance
Raised high in the air as if to wave someone over
Hanging loosely at the sides in a relaxed posture
quiz.e: Akimbo is a hands-on-hips posture.

quiz.q: “Approbation” most closely means
quiz.e: To win someone's approbation is to win their approval.

quiz.q: “Rubicund” most closely means
o: Ruddy or healthy red in color
Pale, thin and sickly in appearance
Rough and rocky, like rugged ground
Golden and bright, like polished metal
quiz.e: Rubicund describes a reddish, healthy complexion.

quiz.q: Which word matches this definition: “a small group that acts together for a shared, often political, purpose”?
quiz.e: A junto is a faction or cabal. An urchin is a mischievous child, a jerkin a short jacket, a flagon a drink container.

quiz.q: Which word matches this definition: “a short, close-fitting, sleeveless jacket”?
quiz.e: A jerkin is a jacket; flagons are containers for drink.

quiz.q: Which word matches: “noisy, boisterous revelers”?
quiz.e: Roysterers party loudly. Adherents are followers; burghers are prosperous townspeople; urchins are mischievous children.

quiz.q: In Keats's poem, “Beadsman” means
o: A man paid or bound to pray for others' souls
A tax collector who serves the Baron's household
A jeweler who makes rosaries for the chapel
A soldier who guards the castle gates at night
quiz.e: The Beadsman counts his beads (rosary) and prays through the cold night.

quiz.q: In “The Haunted Palace”, the word “pinion” (“Never seraph spread a pinion”) most closely means
o: A small tower on a palace wall
A ceremonial robe worn by a king
A jeweled crown set with rubies
quiz.e: A seraph is an angelic being; a pinion is a wing.

quiz.q: In “The Haunted Palace”, “discordant” (“a discordant melody”) most nearly means
o: Peaceful and harmonious, like a lullaby
Ancient and worn, like old stone
Quiet and hushed, as if silent
quiz.e: Discordant is the opposite of harmonious, and it marks the change from the palace's earlier music.

quiz.q: In “Baker's Bluejay Yarn”, “yarn” means
o: A long tale of adventure or incredible happenings, often exaggerated
A type of thread that miners use to mend their heavy equipment and clothing
A written contract between a miner and the buyer of his claim
A scientific study of the behavior of birds in the wild
quiz.e: The class schedule defines yarn this way.

quiz.q: Identify the speaker of: “I am a poor quiet man, a native of the place, and a loyal subject of the King, God bless him!”
quiz.e: Rip says this on his return, not knowing the Revolution has happened, and the crowd shouts "A Tory!"

quiz.q: Identify the person being spoken to in Rip's line above (“I am a poor quiet man ... a loyal subject of the King”).
o: The villagers who crowd around him
Dame Van Winkle, who has come out to the village square to find him
General Washington, who happens to be passing through the village
The strange man with the keg, whom Rip meets again in the village
quiz.e: Rip answers the suspicious crowd that asks whether he is Federal or Democrat.

quiz.q: Identify the speaker of: “Madman! I tell you that she now stands without the door!”
quiz.e: Roderick shrieks this as Madeline appears; the narrator has been reading the Mad Trist.

quiz.q: Identify the person being spoken to in: “Madman! I tell you that she now stands without the door!”
quiz.e: Roderick speaks to his friend the narrator.

quiz.q: Identify the speaker of: “Prithee, put off your journey until sunrise.”
quiz.e: Faith begs her husband not to leave on the night's errand.

quiz.q: Identify the speaker of: “Faith kept me back a while.”
quiz.e: Brown explains why he is late to the traveler he meets in the forest.

quiz.q: In “Come, devil! for to thee is this world given,” who is “thee”?
o: Faith, whom Brown has just lost
Goody Cloyse, the old catechism teacher
Deacon Gookin, on his way to the meeting
quiz.e: Brown, having declared "My Faith is gone!", surrenders to evil.

quiz.q: Identify the speaker of: “Confound it, I don't understand this thing, no way.”
o: The bluejay, as reported by Jim Baker
An owl visiting from Nova Scotia
A miner named Jones from the camp
quiz.e: Baker quotes the jay's speech while telling the yarn.

quiz.q: In “...he believed he could accurately translate any remark which they made,” the pronoun “they” refers to
quiz.e: Twain writes that Baker had studied "his only neighbors, the beasts and the birds".

quiz.q: In Angela's warning to Porphyro (“He curs'd thee and thine, both house and land”), “thee” refers to
quiz.e: Angela tells Porphyro that Hildebrand, in a fever, cursed him and his family.

quiz.q: The best interpretation of “a sense of insufferable gloom pervaded my spirit” (Poe's narrator) is that
o: The house instantly fills him with dread he cannot fully explain
He is happy to see his friend's home again after so many years
He is bored by the long ride and wants to reach the house
He has already seen Madeline's ghost and is afraid of her
quiz.e: Poe builds mood by having the narrator feel gloom before any explicit cause.

quiz.q: The best interpretation of “There is no good on earth; and sin is but a name” (Brown) is that
o: Brown has lost his faith in goodness after the forest revelations
Brown has decided to give up his errand and become a minister
Brown is joking with the traveler to show that he is not afraid
Brown is describing Salem's law code and the punishments it gives
quiz.e: He cries this after "My Faith is gone!" and it foreshadows his later distrust.

quiz.q: The best interpretation of “Mind is the only reality, of which men and all other natures are better or worse reflectors” (Emerson) is that
o: For the idealist, consciousness is the primary reality and the world merely reflects it
Only physical objects are real, and the mind is simply one more object
Society is more real than thought, since it is made of many people
Nature is worthless because the mind can never understand it
quiz.e: The idealist starts from consciousness and reckons the world an appearance.

quiz.q: The best interpretation of “not a dream of motor cars and high wages merely” (Adams) is that
o: The American Dream is meant to be more than material wealth
Cars and high wages are forbidden under the terms of the dream
Only the wealthy can afford to dream in the modern world
The dream is really about the customs of European aristocrats
quiz.e: Adams describes a social order where each person reaches their fullest stature.

quiz.q: The best interpretation of “But evil things, in robes of sorrow, / Assailed the monarch's high estate” (“The Haunted Palace”) is that
o: Forces of decay and misfortune overthrow the ruler and the palace's beauty
The monarch is celebrating a victory over evil forces in his realm
Travelers arrive in robes of sorrow to bring gifts to the palace
A new king takes the throne peacefully in place of the old ruler
quiz.e: The fall of the palace (Thought's dominion) mirrors Roderick's mental collapse.

quiz.q: The best interpretation of “I never see a bird take on so about a little thing” (Baker) is that
o: Baker is humorously observing the jay's human-like temper
Baker is describing an eagle's strength and its power to hunt
Baker is warning listeners about a real danger in the woods
Baker is criticizing bird watchers who disturb the animals
quiz.e: The comment comes as the jay swears over the hole, a comic anthropomorphic moment.

quiz.q: The best interpretation of the new sign, “GENERAL WASHINGTON”, replacing the king's portrait at the inn in “Rip Van Winkle” is that
o: The old monarchy has been replaced by the American republic while Rip slept
Rip has been carried across the ocean to a village somewhere in Europe
The inn's new owner is a retired soldier who admires Washington greatly
Rip has founded a political party named after the general in his absence
quiz.e: The changed sign, flag and political talk show the Revolution has occurred.

quiz.q: The best interpretation of Brown's final gloom, “his dying hour was gloom,” is that
o: The forest experience left him unable to feel hope or trust for the rest of his life
He died happily among family and friends who remembered his goodness and faith
He wrote a cheerful epitaph to comfort the family he was leaving behind
He became a wealthy merchant who forgot the events of that night in the woods
quiz.e: The ending shows the lasting damage of doubt.

quiz.q: The speaker of the Emerson excerpt would most likely AGREE with which statement?
o: Thought and consciousness are more fundamental than material objects or social institutions
Government and society are the highest measure of a person's value and worth
Labor and property are valuable in themselves, apart from any symbolic meaning
Facts and physical evidence alone tell us what is real about the world
quiz.e: Emerson's idealist "does not respect labor ... property" except as symbols of laws of being.

quiz.q: The speaker of the Emerson excerpt would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
o: A person's value is fixed by the mass of their possessions and social rank
The mind is the source of all experience and gives meaning to the world
The world can be seen as a reflection of the consciousness that perceives it
Institutions are important mainly as symbols of larger truths about existence
quiz.e: The idealist judges by the rank things take in consciousness, not size or appearance.

quiz.q: Jim Baker would most likely AGREE with which statement?
o: Bluejays can reason, plan, gossip and feel shame like people
Animals cannot communicate any ideas to one another in any language
Cats are the best talkers among all the birds and beasts of the woods
Jays never swear, however excited they become
quiz.e: Baker says bluejays are the best talkers and have more moods and expressions than other creatures.

quiz.q: Jim Baker would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
o: Bluejays have no sense of humor or memory
Bluejays can outswear even the roughest miner in the whole mining camp
Bluejays remember a good joke and repeat it for years afterward
Bluejays can put every feeling they have into rich, metaphorical language
quiz.e: Baker insists bluejays have humor and memory (jays returned for three years).

quiz.q: The speaker of Adams' passage would most likely AGREE that
o: Everyone should have the opportunity to rise according to ability, regardless of birth
Opportunity should depend mainly on the wealth and family position of the person seeking it
Money and cars are the whole point of the American Dream and its promise
The dream is meant only for people who belong to European upper-class families
quiz.e: Adams says each person should be recognized "regardless of the fortuitous circumstances of birth or position".

quiz.q: The Goodman Brown who returns from the forest would most likely AGREE with which statement?
o: No one, not even the most respected people, can be trusted
Everyone in Salem is honest and faithful to their vows
The devil is a friend to those who seek his company
Faith is always right, so her judgment should be obeyed
quiz.e: Brown becomes a "distrustful" man who turns from his neighbors and wife.

quiz.q: All of the following are true about “Rip Van Winkle” EXCEPT
o: Rip is a strict, hard-working village leader who supports the Revolution
Rip has an insuperable aversion to any kind of profitable labor
Rip sleeps for twenty years in the mountains before he wakes
Rip returns to find his wife dead and his daughter grown
quiz.e: Rip is an idle, good-natured man; he sleeps through the Revolution and is mistaken for a Tory.

quiz.q: All of the following are true about “The Fall of the House of Usher” EXCEPT
o: Madeline dies of an illness and stays permanently in her tomb
Roderick is unusually sensitive to light and sound
The narrator is called to the house by a letter
The house cracks along the fissure and collapses into the tarn
quiz.e: Madeline is entombed but later returns to the door and dies with Roderick.

quiz.q: All of the following are true about “Young Goodman Brown” EXCEPT
o: Brown remains cheerful and trusting for the rest of his life
The story is set in Puritan Salem village in Massachusetts
Brown leaves Faith for an errand in the forest at sunset
Ambiguity remains about whether the forest events were a dream
quiz.e: He becomes "a stern, a sad, a darkly meditative", distrustful man.

quiz.q: All of the following are false about “Baker's Bluejay Yarn” EXCEPT
o: Jim Baker says jays can reason and swear like people
The jay finds a hole in the floor of a mansion in town
The jay understands at once where the acorns must be going
The other jays are silent and serious about the hole
quiz.e: The false statements contradict the text: the hole is in a cabin roof, the jay is baffled, and the crowd laughs.

quiz.q: All of the following are true about “The Eve of St. Agnes” EXCEPT
o: Madeline and Porphyro come from the same friendly family
The poem opens on a bitterly cold night in the winter
The old nurse Angela helps Porphyro reach Madeline's chamber
The lovers flee together into a storm at the end of the poem
quiz.e: Porphyro's family is hostile to Madeline's.

quiz.q: All of the following are true about Washington Irving (Lesson #1 handout) EXCEPT
o: He was born in Boston and never lived abroad
He wrote under the pen name Geoffrey Crayon
He served as United States Minister to Spain in the 1840s
He lived abroad for about seventeen years
quiz.e: Irving was born in Manhattan and spent 17 years in Europe.

quiz.q: All of the following are true about Romanticism (Britannica handout) EXCEPT
o: It stressed order, calm, balance and rationality above emotion
It emphasized the individual, the subjective and the imagination
It reacted against the Enlightenment and eighteenth-century rationalism
It showed a predilection for the exotic, the mysterious and the occult
quiz.e: The handout says Romanticism rejected Classicism's order, calm, harmony, balance and rationality.

quiz.q: All of the following describe direct characterization EXCEPT
o: A character's actions reveal that he is brave
A narrator states, "the patient boy and quiet girl"
A narrator says the woman was "generous"
quiz.e: Actions, speech, thoughts, looks and effect on others are indirect (STEAL).

quiz.q: Which sequence of events in “Rip Van Winkle” is in the correct order?
o: Rip escapes to the mountains; meets the men with the keg; sleeps; wakes to a rusty gun; finds the village changed; meets his daughter
Rip is called a Tory; meets the men with the keg; sleeps; escapes to the mountains; wakes to a rusty gun; meets his daughter
Rip wakes to a rusty gun; escapes to the mountains; meets the men with the keg; sleeps; is called a Tory; meets his daughter
Rip meets his daughter; sleeps; finds the village changed; meets the men with the keg; escapes to the mountains; wakes to a rusty gun
quiz.e: The order follows the plot: mountains, keg, sleep, rusty gun, village, daughter.

quiz.q: Which sequence in “Young Goodman Brown” is correct?
o: Brown leaves Faith at sunset; meets the traveler; sees Goody Cloyse; finds Faith's pink ribbon; attends the forest ceremony; wakes alone
Brown wakes alone; meets the traveler; leaves Faith at sunset; sees Goody Cloyse; finds Faith's pink ribbon; attends the forest ceremony
Brown finds Faith's pink ribbon; leaves Faith at sunset; meets the traveler; wakes alone; sees Goody Cloyse; attends the forest ceremony
Brown attends the forest ceremony; leaves Faith at sunset; meets Goody Cloyse; wakes alone; meets the traveler; finds Faith's pink ribbon
quiz.e: The story moves from Salem street to forest to the morning after.

quiz.q: Which sequence in “The Fall of the House of Usher” is correct?
o: The narrator arrives; Madeline is entombed; a storm rises; the narrator reads the Mad Trist; Madeline appears; the house collapses
The house collapses; Madeline appears; the narrator arrives; a storm rises; Madeline is entombed; the narrator reads the Mad Trist
Madeline appears; the narrator arrives; the Mad Trist is read; a storm rises; Madeline is entombed; the house collapses
The narrator reads the Mad Trist; the narrator arrives; the house collapses; a storm rises; Madeline is entombed; Madeline appears
quiz.e: Poe builds from arrival to entombment to the climax.

quiz.q: Which sequence in “Baker's Bluejay Yarn” is correct?
o: The jay finds the knot-hole; he drops acorns and grows angry; other jays gather; one lands on the open door and sees the acorns; the jays laugh; jays return for three summers
The jays laugh; the jay finds the knot-hole; the crowd gathers; the door is seen open; the jay grows angry; jays return for three summers
The crowd gathers; the jay finds the knot-hole; one jay lands on the door; the first jay laughs; the jay grows angry; jays return for three summers
One jay sees the acorns on the floor; the jay finds the knot-hole; the crowd gathers; the jay grows angry; the jays laugh; jays return for three summers
quiz.e: The discovery of the open door comes after the crowd gathers.

quiz.q: Which sequence of events in “The Eve of St. Agnes” is correct?
o: Porphyro persuades Angela; hides in Madeline's closet; Madeline sleeps; Porphyro sets the feast and plays the lute; she wakes; they flee
The lovers flee; Porphyro hides in the closet; Madeline sleeps; Angela is persuaded; the feast is set; Madeline wakes
Madeline wakes; Angela persuades Porphyro; the feast is prepared; Porphyro hides in the closet; Madeline sleeps; they flee
The lovers flee; Madeline wakes; Porphyro persuades Angela; Porphyro plays the lute; Madeline sleeps; the feast is set
quiz.e: The flight is the poem's climax and comes near the end.

quiz.q: Which order of Irving's life events (Lesson #1 handout) is correct?
o: Born 1783; Salmagundi 1807; History of New-York 1809; Sketch Book 1819-20; Minister to Spain 1842; died 1859
Sketch Book 1819-20; born 1783; Minister to Spain 1842; History of New-York 1809; Salmagundi 1807; died 1859
Born 1783; Minister to Spain 1842; History of New-York 1809; Salmagundi 1807; Sketch Book 1819-20; died 1859
Died 1859; born 1783; Sketch Book 1819-20; Salmagundi 1807; History of New-York 1809; Minister to Spain 1842
quiz.e: The handout gives these dates in this order.

quiz.q: Which order of literary periods from the packet's timeline is correct?
Which statement about Rip's return is accurate?
o: The village has a new inn sign and flag, and villagers ask whether he is Federal or Democrat
The village looks exactly as he left it, with the same old men on the bench at the inn
Rip is greeted as a war hero because he fought bravely at Bunker Hill
His wife welcomes him home at the door with a hot meal and a warm kiss
quiz.e: Irving shows the Revolution's effects on the village through signs, flags and political talk.

quiz.q: Which statement about Dame Van Winkle at the end of the story is accurate?
o: She had died, and Rip learns he is free of her scolding
She became the village postmistress and later the schoolteacher
She waits at the door for him with a warm meal
She fled to New England with Judith after a quarrel
quiz.e: Rip's wife had died of a fit of passion at a peddler, and Rip resumes idle habits.

quiz.q: Which statement about the ninepins players in “Rip Van Winkle” is accurate according to the villagers?
o: They are the ghostly crew of Hendrick Hudson, whose bowling causes the thunder
They are Revolutionary soldiers hiding in the mountains from the British army
They are Dame Van Winkle's relatives, who meet each year on the mountain
They are the village militia, practicing their drills at an old site
quiz.e: Peter Vanderdonk says Hendrick Hudson and his crew of the Halfmoon keep a vigil in the mountains every twenty years (p. 49).

quiz.q: Which statement about Poe's Roderick Usher is accurate?
o: He is unusually sensitive to light, sound and touch and believes the house is somehow sentient
He is a robust athlete who enjoys hunting and other outdoor sports every day
He is a stranger to the narrator and has never before met him in person
He is the narrator's servant, sent ahead to open the mansion for him
quiz.e: Poe emphasizes Roderick's acute senses and nervous condition.

quiz.q: Which statement about the traveler in “Young Goodman Brown” is accurate?
o: He carries a staff like a black snake and claims familiarity with Brown's ancestors
He is Brown's brother, who has come from Boston to bring him home before dark
He carries a cross and a rosary and prays quietly as he walks along the road
He warns Brown to return to Faith and to abandon the errand before it is too late
quiz.e: He says he helped Brown's grandfather and father in acts of Puritan cruelty.

quiz.q: Which statement about Baker's yarn is accurate?
o: Jim Baker is a California miner who says bluejays are the best talkers among birds and beasts
Jim Baker is a Boston scientist who studies birds for a university in the East
Baker says cats are the most intelligent talkers of all the animals he has observed
Baker says animals cannot understand one another and speak only in simple sounds
quiz.e: Twain describes him as a middle-aged, simple-hearted miner.

quiz.q: Which statement about Keats's poem is accurate?
o: The Beadsman prays in the cold at the opening and sleeps “among his ashes cold” at the end
The Beadsman is Porphyro's father and helps him reach Madeline's chamber that night
The poem opens on a summer feast in the Baron's garden, with music and dancing
Madeline is the Beadsman's daughter and lives with him in the cold castle chapel
quiz.e: The Beadsman frames the poem in cold and death.

quiz.q: Which statement about the Emerson excerpt is accurate?
o: It contrasts the materialist, who starts from the external world, with the idealist, who starts from consciousness
It argues for strict Puritan obedience to church and state, above any personal thought or conscience
It praises industry, property and society above thought, intuition and the life of the mind itself
It is a short story about a hunter who wanders alone in the woods at night and meets a stranger
quiz.e: The excerpt is from Emerson's "The Transcendentalist".

quiz.q: What is the effect of Poe's opening description ("dull, dark, and soundless day ... clouds hung oppressively low")?
o: It establishes a gloomy mood and an atmosphere of dread before the house appears
It reveals the ending of the story before the plot has properly begun
It introduces a comic scene to lighten the tone of the whole story
It describes a joyful autumn festival in the countryside near the house
quiz.e: The imagery and diction set the mood.

quiz.q: What does the jay's behavior at the hole show about human nature, according to the yarn?
o: People, like the jay, may stubbornly keep doing something absurd until someone shows them the whole picture
Humans always act logically as soon as they have gathered enough information to decide
Animals are more foolish than humans in almost every situation they face
Hard work is always rewarded in the end, however silly the task may be
quiz.e: The story's humor comes from seeing human faults in animals.

quiz.q: Why does Irving mention that children shout with joy when Rip approaches?
o: It is indirect characterization showing Rip is kind and approachable
It proves that Rip is the village schoolteacher and is paid to teach them
It shows that Rip is a wealthy landowner who gives the children money
It foreshadows his death in the mountains, since the children will mourn him
quiz.e: Effect on others is an indirect characterization technique (STEAL).

quiz.q: What does the pink ribbon Brown sees in the forest suggest?
o: Faith may have been drawn into the evil gathering, threatening his belief in her goodness
The traveler is Brown's father, who has come from the grave to guide him
The forest is safe, since a friendly ribbon shows the way through the dark
Faith left him a small gift to carry with him on his long journey
quiz.e: The ribbon triggers Brown's cry "My Faith is gone!".

quiz.q: Why does the narrator's flight from the house at the end matter to the story's effect?
o: He escapes as the house splits, leaving the image of the tarn closing over the ruins
He inherits the house and its hidden treasure once the last Usher is gone
He confirms that Madeline is alive and well in a village nearby
He returns later to marry Madeline and to restore the ruined estate
quiz.e: The vivid final image completes Poe's unified effect of dread.

quiz.q: What does the swap of the red coat for blue and buff on the inn sign show?
o: That the political world Rip left has changed
That the inn was sold recently to a tailor from the city
That fashion changes quickly in a growing village
That Rip has become rich enough to buy the inn
quiz.e: The symbol reflects the shift from king to Washington.

quiz.q: Why does Keats contrast the cold outside with the warm chamber?
o: To heighten the lovers' warmth and make their world feel fragile against hostility and time
To explain how the Baron's household prepared its rooms for a cold winter night
To criticize the heavy winter clothing worn by the guests at the great feast
To describe the daily work of a farmer during the harshest part of the season
quiz.e: Contrast creates mood.

quiz.q: What does Emerson mean that the idealist "does not respect government, except as far as it reiterates the law of his mind"?
o: The idealist respects institutions only when they reflect truths found in his own mind
The idealist obeys every law without any thought, as a matter of habit
The idealist believes government is the highest truth a person can serve
The idealist wants no laws at all, since laws limit freedom
quiz.e: The excerpt makes consciousness the measure.

quiz.q: A story says, “The old oak groaned and sighed as the wind pushed against it.” This is best labeled
quiz.e: An inanimate object (the tree) is given human traits. Anthropomorphism applies to living beings like animals.

quiz.q: A story says, “The fox pouted, folded his arms, and complained to the crows about the unfairness of the fence.” This is best labeled
quiz.e: A living animal is given human characteristics, as with Baker's jays.

quiz.q: A narrator writes, “Marcus slammed the door and muttered under his breath.” This is best labeled as which type of characterization?
o: Direct, because the narrator states his mood
Symbolic, because the door represents a barrier
Allegorical, because Marcus stands for anger itself
quiz.e: Actions and speech show his mood; the narrator does not simply state his traits.

quiz.q: A narrator writes, “Elena was the most generous person in the village.” This is best labeled as which type of characterization?
quiz.e: The narrator tells us her trait directly.

quiz.q: A poem about a lonely sea captain who hears the ocean whisper his dead wife's name uses which Romantic element most clearly?
o: The supernatural and strong emotion connected to nature
Rationalism and a calm, orderly view of the world around the speaker
Strict classical formality in meter, diction and the arrangement of ideas
Scientific detachment and the careful, unemotional observation of nature
quiz.e: Romanticism values emotion, nature and the mysterious.

quiz.q: A modern writer describes a student who ignores what everyone else thinks and follows her own conscience. Which idea from the unit does this reflect?
quiz.e: Transcendentalism holds that individuals reach truth through intuition.

quiz.q: A student writes, “Twain uses a long, silly story about jays to show that humans can be just as foolish.” This is best described as which type of statement?
o: A plot summary of the story
A vocabulary definition of a term
A quotation with its page citation
quiz.e: It states how the story's device serves a purpose.

quiz.q: A friend says, “Everyone in this town looks holy on Sunday but I've seen them at night.” Which story theme does this most resemble?
o: Hypocrisy in a community, as in “Young Goodman Brown”
Talking animals with human traits, as in Baker's yarn about the jays
Time travel through a very long sleep, as in Rip Van Winkle
A haunted mansion that collapses at the end, as in Usher
quiz.e: Brown sees respected townspeople at the forest ceremony.

quiz.q: What does Rip drink before falling asleep?
o: Liquor from the flagons of the strange men
Tea brewed by his wife and carried up the mountain in a jug
Water from a mountain spring beside the ninepins hollow
Cider from the bowl that Wolf drinks from at home
quiz.e: The keg's liquor, poured into flagons, tastes like "excellent Hollands" (p. 41).

quiz.q: What did Rip's gun look like when he woke?
quiz.e: The rusty fowling-piece is evidence of his long sleep.

quiz.q: What is the name of Rip's dog?
quiz.e: Wolf is as henpecked as his master.

quiz.q: Who is Judith Gardenier?
quiz.e: Rip asks her name and learns she is his daughter; he then says, "I am your father!" (p. 48).

quiz.q: What does Roderick Usher do that makes the narrator uneasy about Madeline's death?
o: He decides to entomb her temporarily in a vault within the house
He buries her at once in the family cemetery beyond the tarn
He has her body cremated on the same night and scatters the ashes
He sends her away to a hospital in the nearest town for treatment
quiz.e: The vault sets up her return.

quiz.q: What object in “Young Goodman Brown” looks like a black snake?
quiz.e: The traveler's staff is compared to a living serpent.

quiz.q: In “The Eve of St. Agnes”, how does Porphyro wake Madeline?
o: By playing an old song on her lute after laying out a feast
By calling her name softly from the door of the chamber
By ringing a chapel bell that echoes through the castle
By opening the curtains so the morning light falls on her face
quiz.e: He plays the ancient ditty "La belle dame sans mercy" on her lute.

quiz.q: In “Baker's Bluejay Yarn”, why do the jays laugh?
o: They see that the jay has been trying to fill a whole house through a hole in the roof
A miner arrives and tells a joke that only the jays seem to understand and enjoy
An owl performs a trick that makes fun of the first jay's mistake in front of them
A cat falls from the roof of the cabin and frightens the whole flock into a wild frenzy
quiz.e: Discovering the acorns on the floor shows the absurdity.

quiz.q: “Rip Van Winkle” is set around the time of
quiz.e: Rip sleeps from British rule to the new republic.

quiz.q: The Salem setting of “Young Goodman Brown” connects to which historical events?
o: The Puritan era, including the Salem witch trials of 1692
The California Gold Rush of the mid-1800s and the mining camps of the West
The Boston Tea Party and the American Revolution that followed it
Reconstruction and the difficult years after the Civil War
quiz.e: Hawthorne's ancestors were involved in Puritan persecution and the trials.

quiz.q: Romanticism developed largely as a reaction against
o: The Romantic movement's own excesses of emotion
Transcendentalism and its focus on the individual
Naturalism and its scientific view of life
quiz.e: The Britannica handout says Romanticism rejected Classicism and reacted against rationalism.

quiz.q: Horace Walpole's The Castle of Otranto (1764) is credited with starting which genre?
quiz.e: The handout traces Gothic literature's origin to Walpole.

quiz.q: Which years does the class schedule ask you to research to understand Twain's yarn?
quiz.e: Twain was born in 1835 and the story was written in 1880.

quiz.q: The Epic of America (1931), where Adams used the phrase "American Dream", was written during which era?
o: The years just after the 1929 stock market crash
The years of the American Revolution and the writing of the Constitution
The time of the Salem witch trials and the Puritan colonies
The years of the Civil War and the debates over slavery
quiz.e: Adams's book appeared as the Great Depression began.

quiz.q: Which historical war is referenced when the traveler says Brown's father burned an Indian village?
quiz.e: The reference points to conflict between Puritan colonists and Native peoples in New England (1675-76).

quiz.q: In “Rip Van Winkle” (p. 35), “the most pestilent little piece of ground in the whole country”: the word “pestilent” most closely means
o: Fertile land that is easy to plow
Holy ground set apart for the church
Remote and hard to reach from town
quiz.e: Context: pestilent means harmful and troublesome; annoying.

quiz.q: In “Rip Van Winkle” (p. 35), “his patrimonial estate had dwindled away”: the word “patrimonial” most closely means
o: Inherited from a father or ancestors
Purchased only recently from a neighbor
Owned by the church of the village
Shared among all the neighbors alike
quiz.e: Context: patrimonial means inherited from a father or ancestors.

quiz.q: In “Rip Van Winkle” (p. 35), “His son Rip, an urchin begotten in his own likeness”: the word “urchin” most closely means
o: An elderly relative from the city
A hired servant on the farm
A stern teacher in the school
quiz.e: Context: urchin means a mischievous small child.

quiz.q: In “Rip Van Winkle” (p. 35), “It could not be from the want of assiduity or perseverance”: the word “assiduity” most closely means
quiz.e: Context: assiduity means constant, careful diligence.

quiz.q: In “Rip Van Winkle” (p. 37), “The opinions of this junto were completely controlled by Nicholas Vedder”: the word “junto” most closely means
o: A small group joined for a shared purpose
A single stubborn person who leads a crowd
A noisy festival held once a year
A legal court that settles village disputes
quiz.e: Context: junto means a small group joined for a shared purpose.

quiz.q: In “Rip Van Winkle” (p. 37), “His adherents, however (for every great man has his adherents)”: the word “adherents” most closely means
quiz.e: Context: adherents means followers or supporters.

quiz.q: In “Rip Van Winkle” (p. 38), “gravely nod his head in token of perfect approbation”: the word “approbation” most closely means
quiz.e: Context: approbation means approval.

quiz.q: In “Rip Van Winkle” (p. 37), “designated by a rubicund portrait of His Majesty George the Third”: the word “rubicund” most closely means
quiz.e: Context: rubicund means ruddy or reddish.

quiz.q: In “Rip Van Winkle” (p. 42), “the grave roysterers of the mountain had put a trick upon him”: the word “roysterers” most closely means
quiz.e: Context: roysterers means noisy, boisterous revelers.

quiz.q: In “Rip Van Winkle” (p. 44), “This desolateness overcame all his connubial fears”: the word “connubial” most closely means
quiz.e: Context: connubial means relating to marriage.

quiz.q: In “Rip Van Winkle” (p. 46), “planting himself before Van Winkle, with one arm akimbo”: the word “akimbo” most closely means
o: Bent with the hand on the hip
Raised high in the air to wave
Hanging limp at the side, tired
Folded behind the back, at ease
quiz.e: Context: akimbo means bent with the hand on the hip.

quiz.q: In “Rip Van Winkle” (p. 40), “Rip complied with his usual alacrity”: the word “alacrity” most closely means
quiz.e: Context: alacrity means brisk, cheerful readiness.

quiz.q: In “Rip Van Winkle” (p. 41), “his heart turned within him, and his knees smote together”: the word “smote” most closely means
o: Froze in the cold mountain air
quiz.e: Context: smote means struck (past tense of smite).

quiz.q: In “Rip Van Winkle” (p. 34), “those men are apt to be obsequious and conciliating abroad, who are under the discipline of shrews at home”: the word “obsequious” most closely means
quiz.e: Context: obsequious means overly eager to please.

quiz.q: In “Rip Van Winkle” (p. 45), “a perfect Babylonish jargon to the bewildered Van Winkle”: the word “jargon” most closely means
o: A song sung by tavern crowds
A blessing spoken over a meal
A proverb handed down by elders
quiz.e: Context: jargon means confusing, hard-to-understand language.

quiz.q: In “Rip Van Winkle” (p. 49), “Peter ... corroborated his story in the most satisfactory manner”: the word “corroborated” most closely means
quiz.e: Context: corroborated means confirmed.

quiz.q: In “Rip Van Winkle” (p. 50), “owing to his having so recently awaked ... during his torpor”: the word “torpor” most closely means
o: A state of inactivity or deep sleep
quiz.e: Context: torpor means a state of inactivity or deep sleep.

quiz.q: In “Young Goodman Brown” (p. 54), “Prithee put off your journey until sunrise”: the word “prithee” most closely means
quiz.e: Context: prithee means i pray you; please.

quiz.q: In “Young Goodman Brown” (p. 54), “she's afeard of herself sometimes”: the word “afeard” most closely means
quiz.e: Context: afeard means afraid.

quiz.q: In “Young Goodman Brown” (p. 56), “I have scruples touching the matter thou wot'st of”: the word “scruples” most closely means
o: Small coins carried for the journey
quiz.e: Context: scruples means moral doubts or hesitations.

quiz.q: In “Young Goodman Brown” (p. 67), “He shrank from the venerable saint as if to avoid an anathema”: the word “anathema” most closely means
o: A friendly greeting from a neighbor
A blessing spoken over a child
quiz.e: Context: anathema means a formal curse or denunciation.

quiz.q: In “Young Goodman Brown” (p. 63), “all the sounds of the benighted wilderness”: the word “benighted” most closely means
o: Famous and well known to travelers
quiz.e: Context: benighted means in darkness (physical or moral).

quiz.q: In “Young Goodman Brown” (p. 66), “hoary-bearded elders ... have whispered wanton words to the young maids”: the word “wanton” most closely means
quiz.e: Context: wanton means immoral or unrestrained.

quiz.q: In “The Fall of the House of Usher” (p. 88), “its uncouth and unimaginative prolixity”: the word “prolixity” most closely means
quiz.e: Context: prolixity means tiresome length or wordiness.

quiz.q: In “The Fall of the House of Usher” (p. 72), “a barely discernible fissure”: the word “fissure” most closely means
o: A window set into the wall
A shadow cast by the roof
quiz.e: Context: fissure means a crack or narrow opening.

quiz.q: In “The Fall of the House of Usher” (p. 70), “a black and lurid tarn”: the word “tarn” most closely means
o: A tomb dug into the hillside
quiz.e: Context: tarn means a small mountain lake.

quiz.q: In “The Fall of the House of Usher” (p. 71), “a cadaverousness of complexion”: the word “cadaverousness” most closely means
quiz.e: Context: cadaverousness means corpse-like paleness.

quiz.q: In “Baker's Bluejay Yarn” (p. 140), “got off as many leather-headed opinions as an average crowd of humans”: the word “leather-headed” most closely means
quiz.e: Context: leather-headed means stupid or thick-headed.

quiz.q: Identify the speaker: “Poor Wolf, thy mistress leads thee a dog's life of it; but never mind, my lad, whilst I live thou shalt never want a friend to stand by thee!” (p. 38)
quiz.e: Rip speaks to his dog.

quiz.q: Identify the person being spoken to in the line above (“Poor Wolf ...”).
quiz.e: Rip shares his wallet with Wolf as a fellow-sufferer.

quiz.q: Identify the speaker: “Nicholas Vedder! Why, he is dead and gone these eighteen years.” (p. 46)
o: The man in the cocked hat
quiz.e: An old man answers Rip's question in a thin, piping voice.

quiz.q: Identify the person being spoken to: “Where's Van Brummel, the school-master?” — “He went off to the wars, too; was a great militia general, and is now in Congress.” The person being spoken to in the answer is
quiz.e: The villager answers Rip's questions about old friends.

quiz.q: Identify the speaker: “Ah, poor man, Rip Van Winkle was his name, but it's twenty years since he went away from home with his gun.” (p. 48)
o: An old woman in the crowd
quiz.e: Rip has just asked the woman with a child her name and her father's name.

quiz.q: Identify the speaker: “It is Rip Van Winkle—it is himself. Welcome home again, old neighbor.” (p. 48)
o: An old woman who peers under her hand at his face
Judith Gardenier, who has just learned his name
Dame Van Winkle, who has somehow come back from the grave to greet him
The self-important man in the cocked hat, who had questioned him harshly
quiz.e: An old woman recognizes him before Peter Vanderdonk arrives.

quiz.q: In Rip's cry “that's me yonder—no—that's somebody else, got into my shoes” (p. 47), the person “yonder” is
o: His son, young Rip, who looks like him
The stranger with the keg who led him up the mountain
Peter Vanderdonk, the oldest man in the village
quiz.e: Rip sees a counterpart of himself leaning against the tree.

quiz.q: Identify the speaker: “You are late, Goodman Brown. The clock of the Old South was striking as I came through Boston.” (pp. 54-55)
o: The traveler with the serpent-like staff
Deacon Gookin, riding along the road on horseback toward the meeting
Goody Cloyse, on her way to the meeting
The minister of Salem village, on his way to the forest gathering
quiz.e: Brown answers, "Faith kept me back a while."

quiz.q: Identify the speaker: “Ah, forsooth, and is it your worship indeed?” (p. 58)
quiz.e: She greets the traveler, whom she calls her old gossip's image.

quiz.q: Identify the person being spoken to: “Ah, forsooth, and is it your worship indeed?”
o: Goodman Brown, hiding in the woods
quiz.e: Goody Cloyse speaks to the traveler after he touches her neck with the serpent staff.

quiz.q: Identify the speaker: “Welcome, my children, to the communion of your race.” (p. 65)
o: The dark figure in the shape of a grave divine (the devil)
The minister of Salem village, leading the forest congregation in prayer
Deacon Gookin, leading the ceremony beside the blazing altar-rock
Goodman Brown, greeting the converts who stand beside him
quiz.e: He addresses the converts, Brown and Faith.

quiz.q: Identify the person being spoken to in “Faith! Faith! look up to heaven, and resist the wicked one.” (p. 67)
quiz.e: Brown speaks to his wife at the altar.

quiz.q: Identify the speaker: “What God doth the wizard pray to?” (p. 67)
o: The minister, taking his morning walk
Faith, at the window of the house
quiz.e: Brown hears Gookin's morning prayer and reacts in suspicion.

quiz.q: Identify the speaker: “We have put her living in the tomb!” (p. 90)
quiz.e: Roderick confesses that he heard Madeline's movements in the coffin.

quiz.q: Identify the person being spoken to in Roderick's speech “Not hear it?—yes, I hear it, and have heard it.” (p. 90)
quiz.e: The narrator bends close to hear the gibbering words.

quiz.q: Identify the speaker: “Hello, I reckon I've struck something.” (p. 138)
o: The bluejay, as quoted by Jim Baker
Jim Baker's neighbor from the camp
quiz.e: Baker reports the jay's words as the acorn rolls off the roof.

quiz.q: Identify the speaker: “Come here, everybody; hang'd if this fool hasn't been trying to fill up a house with acorns!” (p. 141)
o: An old jay who lands on the open door
Jim Baker, watching from his cabin
The first jay, at last understanding his error
The owl from Nova Scotia, passing through
quiz.e: He finds the acorns on the floor.

quiz.q: In Twain's “I knew he could, however, because he told me so himself,” the pronoun “he” refers to
quiz.e: The narrator refers to the miner who says he understands animals (p. 137).

quiz.q: In Twain's “the whole absurdity of the contract that that first jay had tackled hit him home,” “him” refers to
o: Each jay that lands on the door and looks inside
The narrator, who tells the story from a distance in time and place
Jim Baker, who watches the whole scene from the door of his cabin
Only the first jay, who made the original mistake and is embarrassed
quiz.e: Each new jay understands the joke when he sees the acorns (p. 141).

quiz.q: In Irving's “he had got his neck out of the yoke of matrimony,” “he” refers to
quiz.e: Rip is glad that Dame's government has ended (p. 50).

quiz.q: According to the Introduction, in what year and place did Poe publish “Metzengerstein”, using the technique of the single effect?
o: 1839, in Burton's Gentleman's Magazine, as a story of the doomed house
1819, in The Sketch Book, as a tale of a gloomy old hall
1880, in A Tramp Abroad, as a tale of a strange animal
quiz.e: The Introduction (p. 9) dates it to January 14, 1832.

quiz.q: According to the Introduction, who "together created the short story as a form"?
quiz.e: The editors credit Poe and Hawthorne together.

quiz.q: The Introduction contrasts Irving's tale with Poe's. Which description matches Irving's “Rip Van Winkle”?
o: An orderly tale of linked incidents chronologically treated, graceful, humorous and urbane
A concentrated tale of a single preconceived effect, aimed at one climactic moment and a controlled mood
A tale of ratiocination, in which patient reasoning solves a mystery and reveals the truth of a crime
A tale of local color, set in a gold camp with colorful and contradictory characters and rough humor
quiz.e: Poe's alternative is the concentrated tale of effect (p. 11).

quiz.q: Which term describes Poe's technique in the Introduction?
o: The concentrated tale of a single, preconceived effect
A long chronological chronicle of many linked incidents told in order
A tale of local color rooted in the speech and customs of a single region
An animal fable in which the creatures teach a lesson about human behavior
quiz.e: The action is focused on the climactic moment and the mood is controlled from first to last.

quiz.q: In the Introduction, what does “specific gravity” (Henry Seidel Canby's phrase) refer to?
o: The moral or intellectual weight Hawthorne added to the American story
The physical weight of a printed anthology on a shelf or a classroom desk
A measure of how long a story runs from beginning to end in pages
The number of villains that a story places against its main character
quiz.e: The editors say the typical American story asks to be taken seriously.

quiz.q: According to the Introduction, the settings of “The Fall of the House of Usher” and “Young Goodman Brown” are similar because both
o: Move from light into darkness and back into light on a journey and return
Take place in the American West among miners, outlaws and desert travelers
Are narrated by talking animals with human traits and a sense of humor
Take place inside a single room over the course of one long evening
quiz.e: Both are built on a journey and a return (p. 14).

quiz.q: According to the Introduction, how does Hawthorne's darkness differ from Poe's?
o: Hawthorne's is the darkness of the soul; Poe's is the theatrical dark of the horror tale
Hawthorne's is comic and light in tone; Poe's is scientific and detached
Hawthorne's is set in daylight scenes; Poe's is set in a dark cave
The two kinds of darkness are identical in every important respect
quiz.e: The editors call Hawthorne's forest the forest of sin and evil.

quiz.q: According to the Introduction, which statement about Twain is accurate?
o: He never wrote a good short story, but mastered the humorous frontier sketch and the fable
He is the greatest short story writer in history and stands well above Poe
He invented the Gothic tale and taught Poe its most important methods
He wrote only poetry and never attempted prose fiction of any length
quiz.e: The editors say “Bluejay Yarn” is superb in its own kind (p. 19).

quiz.q: The Introduction links “Baker's Bluejay Yarn” to which other work?
o: Joel Chandler Harris's Uncle Remus stories
quiz.e: Both are beast stories, and Thurber's fables are named later (pp. 19-20).

quiz.q: The Introduction says Poe's phrase for his terror was
o: “not of Germany but of the soul”
quiz.e: The editors then judge that his effects seem no deeper than gooseflesh (p. 12).

quiz.q: The Introduction names which Poe story as Poe at his best?
o: “The Fall of the House of Usher”
quiz.e: The editors point to the doomed mansion and the inverted image of the house in the tarn (p. 13).

quiz.q: The Introduction says Poe's tale of ratiocination is the parent of which genre?
quiz.e: Its example is “The Murders in the Rue Morgue”.

quiz.q: According to the Introduction, which two Irving works are named as his best and best known?
o: “Rip Van Winkle” and “The Legend of Sleepy Hollow”
quiz.e: The editors say he never bettered them (p. 10).

quiz.q: The editors' criteria for choosing stories were the excellence of each story and its
o: Representativeness in the development of the story in the United States
Length, so that each selected story fits on a single spread of pages
Popularity in magazines during the writer's own lifetime and afterward
Use as a model in classroom writing exercises for young students
quiz.e: The Introduction says the criteria were double (p. 10).

quiz.q: What kind of story does the Introduction say Hawthorne began writing?
o: A story that probes an exposed situation rather than linking incidents or contriving effects
A comic yarn about animals with human traits, told in a folksy voice by a narrator
A detective puzzle solved by a clever amateur who follows a trail of reasoning and clues
A travelogue that records, in a plain style, a long journey through unfamiliar country
quiz.e: The Introduction links this to Henry James's idea of a situation revealed (p. 15).

quiz.q: On his return, what does Rip learn about Nicholas Vedder and Van Brummel? (p. 46-47)
o: Vedder died eighteen years ago and Van Brummel became a militia general and a member of Congress
Both moved to New York City to start new businesses in trade after the war ended
Both became innkeepers in neighboring villages along the river and grew rich
Both are still on the bench at the inn, talking about the news of the day as before
quiz.e: The answers show "enormous lapses of time" and unfamiliar matters like war and Congress.

quiz.q: Why is Rip called “A Tory! A spy! A refugee!” in the village? (p. 46)
o: He says he is a loyal subject of the King when the town has just fought a revolution
He carries a British flag through the village square as he asks for old friends
He refuses to say how he would vote in the election that day
He demands to see the mayor on his very first day back in town
quiz.e: His loyalty statement is out of date.

quiz.q: What is Irving's tone when he says Rip "had got his neck out of the yoke of matrimony"? (p. 50)
o: Humorous and ironic, celebrating Rip's escape from petticoat government
Solemn and tragic, mourning the loss of Rip's long marriage to Dame
Enraged, condemning the whole institution of marriage in the village
Scientific, recording facts about Rip's life without any comment
quiz.e: Irving jokes that Rip has escaped the only despotism that troubled him.

quiz.q: What do henpecked husbands in the neighborhood wish for, according to the last paragraph of “Rip Van Winkle”? (p. 51)
o: A quieting draught out of Rip Van Winkle's flagon
A new farm far away from their wives and their many duties
A trip to England to see the King and his court in person
A seat in the new Congress in the young capital of the country
quiz.e: Irving ends with a comic tribute to the flagon.

quiz.q: Which best states what Peter Vanderdonk tells the crowd? (p. 49)
o: Hendrick Hudson and his crew of the Halfmoon keep a vigil in the Kaatskills every twenty years
Rip stole a boat from the harbor many years ago and sailed away to sea and was lost
Rip served in the Continental Army under General Washington in the war and was wounded
The mountains are safe and free of any legends or strange visitors, and never were haunted
quiz.e: He corroborates Rip's story.

quiz.q: Identify the sequence in “Young Goodman Brown” from the text (pp. 54-67).
o: Faith asks him to stay; the traveler joins him; Goody Cloyse is touched by the staff; a pink ribbon falls; the altar ceremony; Brown wakes alone
The altar ceremony; Faith asks him to stay; the traveler joins him; a pink ribbon falls; Goody Cloyse is touched by the staff; Brown wakes alone
The traveler joins him; the altar ceremony; Faith asks him to stay; a pink ribbon falls; Goody Cloyse is touched by the staff; Brown wakes alone
A pink ribbon falls; the traveler joins him; Faith asks him to stay; Goody Cloyse is touched by the staff; the altar ceremony; Brown wakes alone
quiz.e: The order follows the story.

quiz.q: Which claim about the traveler in “Young Goodman Brown” is accurate? (p. 56)
o: He says he helped Brown's grandfather lash a Quaker woman and Brown's father burn an Indian village
He says Brown's family never once set foot in the forest or took part in any violence
He says the ministers of Salem are his bitter enemies and have driven him from town
He says he is Faith's father and has come to fetch her home before the meeting begins
quiz.e: This challenges Brown's claim that his ancestors were "honest men and good Christians".

quiz.q: What does the traveler do to Goody Cloyse with his staff? (p. 58)
o: Touches her neck with what seems the serpent's tail, and she recognizes him as the devil
Strikes her with it to drive her from the path and away from the meeting
Gives it to her as a gift so that she can walk more easily
Breaks it in half to show that he means no harm to anyone
quiz.e: Then he throws it at her feet and she disappears.

quiz.q: What does Brown see at the forest meeting? (p. 63-65)
o: A blazing altar-like rock and a congregation including the minister, Deacon Gookin and Goody Cloyse
A quiet prayer meeting of unfamiliar travelers who have come from far away to worship in the woods
A market where merchants sell their goods by torchlight in a clearing in the forest at night
A battlefield where the soldiers of two armies fight through the night beside a burning barn
quiz.e: He recognizes the pious townspeople among the worshippers.

quiz.q: What does the dark figure say about the townspeople? (p. 65-66)
o: That all whom Brown has revered are in his worshipping assembly and Brown will learn their secret deeds
That they are innocent victims of an evil plot that was made against them by their enemies in the woods
